text:
Maria: heads-up — after last night's kernel-selection tweak we saw a reproducible increase in KV cache paging for long-ctx workloads (1000+ tokens). memory climbs ~20% over 2 min and fragmentation spikes. stack traces point at cross-segment lock hold times during prefix lookups.
Ken: ack. any flamegraphs / profiles? can you paste the perf top or pprof?
Maria: pasted a short flame snippet, here's the main hotspot:
```
  kv::lookup_prefix
    -> kv::acquire_segment_lock (50% CPU)
    -> kernel_selector::score_path
```
The segment lock appears to be contended when multiple requests probe nearby prefixes.
Sam: is this the same failure mode as the session-sticky experiment we ran (prefetch handoff)? looks similar to earlier contention but different caller.
Maria: similar surface, different root. earlier we had long-lived sticky sessions keeping pages resident; this is cross-request reuse where hash collisions + probing cause long linear scans under the lock. eviction thrashing then triggers paging.
Alex: curious — kernel change changed the ordering of probe paths? could alter cache key access pattern and increase hot-span overlap.
Ken: what does the cache key look like now? any added entropy or salt?
Maria: current key: `tenant|model|prefix-fingerprint|session-id?` we started appending a runtime variant tag after the kernel change (was meant to help routing). that expanded keyspace and moved some common prefixes into different segments, causing more cross-segment probes.
Sam: two quick mitigations to try: 1) revert runtime-variant tag from key (cheap), 2) add a short-granularity session affinity hint (sticky hint) to keep reuse local. also suggest bumping eviction target from 70% -> 60% to ease thrash while we fix.
Alex: +1 on temporary revert. long-term we should make key derivation stable wrt kernel routing: separate routing tag from cache fingerprint (i.e., cache_fingerprint = hash(tenant, model, prefix) and routing_tag only used for placement).
Ken: agree. also we can add a per-segment probe budget to avoid holding the global lock during long scans — do a best-effort decode to an alternate segment instead of blocking.
Maria: ran a quick canary: reverted runtime tag locally + bumped eviction aggressiveness. after 30s run memory growth is flat and fragmentation dropped ~40%. still need more runs.
CI Bot: deploy/1729 completed to canary (eng-runtime/canary).
Sam: can you share the exact config you used? I'll reproduce on my rig.
Maria: config snippet:
```
kv.cache.key_format = "tenant|model|prefix_fingerprint"
kv.eviction.target_fill = 0.60
kv.probe.max_steps = 64
kv.session_hint.ttl = 10s
```
Ken: once we confirm, follow ups: - hygiene: audit other codepaths that append ephemeral tags to keys - instrumentation: add per-segment probe histogram + lock hold time metric - experiment: try probe-skipping policy that yields after N checks and requeues a lightweight prefetch.
Alex: I'll own the key-derivation change and instrument the probe histograms. Sam/Ken can own the canary reproduce + probe budget experiment. Maria can coordinate rollout.
Maria: thanks — leaving the canary running, will post perf dump at +1h. adding action items to the runtime board. :thumbsup:
